facts.statement: The genus Muyelensaurus was named in 2007 by paleontologists Jorge Calvo, Bernardo González Riga, and Juan Porfiri.
facts.quote: The name Muyelensaurus first appeared in a 2007 paper by Argentine paleontologists Jorge Calvo of the Universidad Nacional del Comahue and Bernardo González Riga of the Laboratorio de Paleovertebrados, and Brazilian paleontologist Juan Porfiri of the Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro.

facts.statement: Muyelensaurus is a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Muyelensaurus (meaning "Muyelen lizard", after an indigenous name for the Colorado River in Argentina) is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina.

facts.statement: Muyelensaurus was more slender than other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: It was more slender than other titanosaurs.

facts.statement: Fossils of Muyelensaurus were found in the Neuquén province of Patagonia, originally assigned to the Portezuelo Formation but later reclassified to the Plottier Formation.
facts.quote: Fossils have been recovered in the Neuquén province of Patagonia and were originally assigned to the Portezuelo Formation but further research showed that these layers belong to the Plottier Formation.

facts.statement: A unique feature of Muyelensaurus is that the basal tuber of its braincase has a divergence angle of a right angle.
facts.quote: Autapomorphic to Muyelensaurus was the basal tuber of the braincase having a divergence angle that was a right angle.

facts.statement: Some studies place Muyelensaurus as a basal member of the Lithostrotia.
facts.quote: The cladogram below follows Franca et al. (2016), placing Muyelensaurus as a basal lithostrotian.

facts.statement: Other studies place Muyelensaurus within the clade Rinconsauria.
facts.quote: The cladogram below follows Mocho et al. (2019), this time placing Muyelensaurus within Rinconsauria.

facts.statement: Muyelensaurus pecheni lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 89 million years ago, between the Turonian and Coniacian stages.
facts.quote: Muyelensaurus pecheni es la única especie conocida del género extinto Muyelensaurus es un género de dinosaurio saurópodo saltasáurido, que vivió a finales del Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 89 millones de años entre el Turoniense y Coniaciense en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Fossils of Muyelensaurus were discovered by paleontologist Jorge Calvo at Loma Lindero in Rincón de los Sauces, Neuquén, Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles fueron descubiertos por el paleontólogo Jorge Calvo en la Loma Lindero, en Rincón de los Sauces, pertenecientes a la Formación Portezuelo, en Neuquén, Patagonia Argentina.

facts.statement: The fossil remains of Muyelensaurus include the base of the skull, cervical, dorsal, sacral, and caudal vertebrae, as well as numerous limb bones.
facts.quote: Los restos incluyen la base del cráneo, vértebras cervicales, dorsales, sacras y caudales, así como numerosos huesos de los miembros.

facts.statement: Muyelensaurus is characterized by autapomorphies including basal tuber divergences of 70 degrees, a concave thin lamina uniting basal tuberosities ventrally, a basioccipital condyle sharing the proximal portion of the basal tuberosity, posterior dorsal neural spines with a long pre-spinal lamina reinforced by two accessory laminae, and a distal pubic ramus that is rectangular and medially curved.
facts.quote: Es caracterizado por la siguiente asociación de autapomorfias, las bases de las tuberosidades divergen 70 grados uno del otro; Una lámina cóncava y delgada une a las tuberosidades basales ventralmente, el cóndilo basioccipital comparte la porción proximal de la tuberosidad basal; las espinas neurales dorsales de la parte posterior posee una larga lámina preespinal reforzada por dos laminas accesorias, la porción distal del final de la rama púbica es rectangular y medialmente curvado.

facts.statement: A cladistic analysis placed Muyelensaurus pecheni and Rinconsaurus caudamirus in a new group within the Lithostrotia called Rinconsauria.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico de la filogenia ha ubicado al Muyelensaurus pecheni y a Rinconsaurus caudamirus como un nuevo grupo dentro de los Lithostrotia y llamaron al clado Rinconsauria.

facts.statement: Muyelensaurus lived from the Coniacian to the Santonian, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Santonian (89.8 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Recent research suggests that fossil material previously attributed to Muyelensaurus pecheni may belong to sauropods from more than one taxon, potentially restricting the species to the holotype specimen only.
facts.quote: Pérez Moreno et al. (2026) revise the fossil material attributed to Muyelensaurus pecheni, interpret it as belonging to sauropods from more than one taxon, and restrict M. pecheni to the holotype specimen only.
